title: TypeScript SDK: robust async-iterable <-> Web Streams interop patterns and examples
creator: Marcus Nguyen
description: Deliver a small set of ergonomic, well-tested interop patterns and end-to-end examples that make the TypeScript SDK first-class for streaming use cases across Node (AsyncIterator / ReadableStream), Deno, and browser Web Streams. The goal is to standardize cancel/backpressure semantics, provide minimal adapters, and publish examples and tests that demonstrate common real-world flows (single consumer, dual consumer/tee, resumable reconnect with cursor, and cancellation with AbortSignal).
proposal: Adopt a canonical pull-based AsyncIterator surface in the SDK and ship three lightweight adapters: 1) asyncIterableToReadableStream(node/browser polyfill), 2) readableStreamToAsyncIterable, and 3) teeWithSharedKVcache for safe dual-consume patterns. Provide explicit AbortSignal propagation and standardized chunk framing helpers. Maintain a small set of top-level recipes in the repo: node-server example, deno-worker example, and browser fetch+stream demo. Keep API surface minimal to avoid maintenance overhead but provide extensibility hooks for advanced teams.
decision_rationale: Reasons: 1) AsyncIterator is the most ergonomic for Node and TypeScript consumers; 2) Web Streams are native in browser/Deno and are required for first-class browser SDK demos; 3) explicit AbortSignal propagation avoids subtle cancellation leaks; 4) conservative memory usage (no hidden buffering) is aligned with Dedicated and Private use cases where memory/performance matters. Alternatives considered: making ReadableStream the canonical surface (rejected because Node consumers prefer async iteration) and a heavy shim that auto-retries reads (rejected due to complexity and potential duplicate tokens).
implementation_notes:
- Add adapter module under src/streams/interop.ts with clear exported helpers.
- Ensure adapters are pure TypeScript and tree-shakeable.
- Use a tiny framing helper (src/streams/frame.ts) to support chunked messages and delimiting for both text and binary chunks.
- Hook AbortSignal into both underlying fetch requests and iterator cancellation paths.
- Provide examples in examples/streams/{node,deno,browser} with README and an automated e2e test.
- Update SDK docs and changelog.
- Add runtime checks to detect double-consume and surface a clear error message with guidance to use teeWithSharedKVcache.
acceptance_criteria:
- Adapters exist and compile cleanly in Node/Deno/browser toolchains.
- Unit tests cover cancellation propagation, backpressure (simulated slow consumers), dual-consume failure mode, and tee-based dual-consume success.
- End-to-end examples reproduce a streaming chat scenario in Node, Deno, and browser.
- Benchmarks show additional per-chunk latency <5ms and <1MB memory overhead per active stream on our CI baseline.
- Docs and three example recipes merged to main and linked from SDK README.
- One RFC-style doc published in the repo describing semantics and recommended patterns.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Consumers will misuse adapters and create memory leaks (e.g., reading into arrays). Mitigation: enforce streaming-only helper APIs; document anti-patterns.
- Risk: Race conditions when teeing live streams. Mitigation: implement a small ring buffer with backpressure propagation and exhaustive tests.
- Risk: Browser polyfills diverge from Node behavior. Mitigation: CI runs tests in Node 18, Deno stable, and Chromium headless.
- Risk: API churn if we later change canonical surface. Mitigation: keep adapters internal-first but publish stable examples; deprecate with clear migration path if needed.
test_plan:
- Unit tests: interop adapters, framing helpers, abort propagation, and tee ring buffer.
- Integration tests: example workflows launched in CI (Node 18, Deno, Chromium).
- Load test: synthetic stream fan-out to ensure memory and latency targets.
- Fuzz tests: malformed framing boundaries and partial chunks.
- Observability: add test hooks that emit timing markers so we can assert <5ms overhead in CI.
- QA checklist included in PR template for the feature.
